en: Without faltering against the Burut,
Let those who will wreak wondrous slaughter come,
Of the damned Burut,
Bind their strong ones and bring them,
Kill their weak ones and return.
Gather their warriors,
Slaughter them as sacrifices and return,
Drag them onto the road,
Split them open for the great dogs and return.
Their twelve-year-old blood-shedder,
If Manas falls into your hands,
Without killing or losing him,
Capture him and bring him alive!
Let us have our fill of sport,
That damned blood-shedder,
Let us use him as a stud for the girls.
If a male child is born of Manas,
Putting my golden crown on him,
Without reproach, without dispute,
Seating him on the golden throne,
The child born of him,
Let us raise him as khan.
If you fail to capture him,
You will see terrible wrath,
With your arm armor spreading wide,
Every one of your khans
Will die at Manas's hands alone.
He was born in Altai,
Should he live, you will see,
He will bring turmoil to Beejin.
It is entered in our register,
If he matures and becomes a man,
That Manas, grown up,
If he equals a warrior's son,
If he attacks, this head will be lost.
If he matures and becomes a man,
If he equals a warrior's son,
The khanship of this Beejin,
Should he live, he will contest.
He will raid your horses without ceasing,
Driving you off in terror,
He will slaughter your people,
Beejin of Chynmachyn,
He will make your people shriek.
This Beejin where no deluge reaches,
He is the boy whose force will reach it,
Beejin that Iskender could not reach,
He is the boy whose deeds will reach it.
His courage is different, his wrath is fierce,
Sparing no life that grapples with him,
He levels whoever attacks.
His bulk is like half a mountain,
That ill-omened Burut
Seems ready to devour whoever attacks.
That Manas is truly Manas
Has become known to all the people,
When that Manas was born,
‘He will wreak havoc,’ it said,
‘Of light-bathed Beejin,
He will seize the khanship,’
It was inscribed in the register.
His name, into the Beejin Kakan's
Register, had already passed,
When Manas was being born,
Through this very Beejin
An earthquake swept once.
When told, ‘Capture Manas and bring him,’
All my sorcerers were mistaken,
They all saw only part,
My wrath rose and I stood rigid,
All my sorcerers
Today have died at my hands.
Mighty ones wearing armor,
Understand what I say,
Do not let Manas go free,
All you champions, heed my words,
If he falls into your hands, bind him and bring him.
The damned Kyrgyz of forty households,
‘My boy's name is Madman,’ he said,
The cunning Burut kept him hidden,
Through guile, his wickedness,
How that Burut has made it succeed,
‘My boy's name is Madman,’ he said,
How that Burut has concealed him!
Coming to Altai and running wild,
If Manas grows up tomorrow,
He will devouringly slaughter my people,
If Manas becomes a man tomorrow,
He will set the grasslands ablaze,
Slaughtering straight across Beejin,
He will set fire to the meadows,
He will not let us settle in Beejin,
That damned blood-shedder,
If he grows up, will leave us no peace.
The reason he will leave us no peace—
Driven out from Chet-Beejin,
His migration was broken by us men of Beejin.
We killed his seven forefathers,
We bound their hands and feet,
We subjected them all to humiliation,
Such is the vengeance Manas bears.
Boar-natured hero Zholoy,
My kaldai clad in arm armor,
Who does not draw back from fire,
My mighty champion Döngö,
To capture Manas and bring him,
To place him truly in my hands,
You have proven, skilled champions,
Who truly do not fear death,
Like iron tempered to perfection,
Your bulk like half a mountain,
Not one alone, but a multitude of you,
With the forms of lions,
My champions, you are all here!
Khan Zholoy of the Kalmyks,
Your prowess is extraordinary,
Your heroism is great,
When you rode on campaign in mellow autumn,
You leveled the hill that opposed you.
Once on the slopes of great Kap-Too,
At the edge of Suuk-Tör,
You wrought devastating feats of valor,
Fighting the giants,
Iron-eared giant Kutan,
Iron-browed giant Mangkush,
Iron-naveled giant Kiten,
Giant Kazan riding Karager,
Scissor-eared giant Kaman,
You conquered Kap-Too and made it your land,
You bound five giants and made them subjects.
Your world lacked nothing,
Giants of lesser stature,
You were a hero who brought them bound,
Among so many Kytay,
You were the one I trusted.
You were a son of the Black Kalmyks,
You were a house built on a mountain slope,
You alone, my mighty one,
Had the strength of a thousand champions.
Eating seven batmans of wheat,
You were a servant smelling of grain,
Killing seventy giants,
You were a son smelling of blood,
Eating eight batmans of wheat,
You were a servant smelling of grain,
Killing eighty warriors,
You were a son smelling of blood.
Sparing none who grappled with you,
You still have a champion's form,
Your name is Zholoy, a mighty name,
Can such a one arise among men,
A giant-creature like you?
In the city of Chet-Beejin
I have no warrior like you,
In Kakanchyn, in Beejin,
You are the support I have firmly bound.
‘He is fit to stand against them,’ I say,
You are the warrior I have trusted.
When dawn spreads clear and white,
When light enters the land,
When the true dawn breaks,
When dawn has grown bright,
An army of countless men beneath seven banners,
Let me gather them fully,
From Chynmachyn, from Beejin,
Let me gather true champions,
Let us make them file past,
Let us choose their warriors.
Set your appointed time for dawn,
Take a sure champion as companion,
If you find the means, kill him and return,
If you have the cunning, Manas,
Bring him bound alive in the end!
Döngö, Zholoy, my champions,
Your strife reaches the whole world,
If in combat your strength falls short,
If you two return empty-handed,
Do not appear before my eyes,
Do not come near me!
If your strength is no match for Manas,
If you return empty-handed, my champion,
I shall cut off your head with a sword,
Every one of you, without delay,
I shall slaughter!
If you cannot prevail in combat,
If you let Manas escape,
The worst of all calamities—
I shall have your pit dug deep,
I shall bring to the boil, champions,
Your far-off misfortune!
I shall heap thick torment upon you,
Tying a rope around your neck,
I shall have you hauled to the physician,
I shall have your head cut off with a sword,
I shall have great suffering inflicted!
My champions, consider,
If you do not do exactly as I say,
I shall leave not one of you alive!”
He had the giants Döngö and Zholoy,
He had gathered his extraordinary giants,
That mighty Esenkan.
The war drum was beaten hard,
When they heard the war drum's sound,
The many seething champions
Crowded in upon Esenkan,
A multitude of swarming beings,
Whose speech no man could understand,
With a single eye in their heads,
A thousand of these came,
To bring Manas back bound,
He assigned them to hero Döngö.
Those champions he assigned—
Skilled riders, swift runners,
They had forms unlike mortal men,
When they attacked, they wrought great havoc.
From beyond them,
Those who bound with cords,
Of those who entered combat,
Not a thread of life remained,
Among those champions,
Skilled riders, swift runners,
The champions Orko and Kerke,
Taking orders from their khan,
Set out together with them.
One group of champions
Had skill in casting lassos,
Another group of champions
Had masters of the battle-axe.
Among those champions,
Those with nets of iron rope,
Who would swarm upon a man,
And encircle him,
All with daggers in their hands,
Cunning among spearmen,
Their pitiless masters,
Of all the champions,
Zholoy and Döngö were the finest,
Their mighty men wearing armor,
Their heroes wearing mail,
Who roared when angered,
Their infidels who wrought havoc,
Taking orders from their khan,
The champions were to set out,
Making ready in Chong-Beejin.
There were rhinoceroses and elephants,
There were mules and camels,
Of the seething infidels,
There were giants on every side.
To capture Manas and bring him,
To their Chylaba Esenkan,
To capture him alive and deliver him,
A tumult rose, an army flooded forth,
Not a small number, but a vast flood,
The sight distracted the mind,
The champions' clubs
Looked like small travel tents,
